questions.text: R त्रिज्या के वृत्ताकार वलय के रूप में एक पतली प्लास्टिक छड़ को मोड़ा गया है। इसे आवेश घनत्व σ से एकसमान आवेशित किया गया है। इसके केंद्र पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र का परिमाण है:
questions.text_english: A thin plastic rod is bent into a circular ring of radius R. It is uniformly charged with charge density σ. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zero. A uniformly charged circular ring has a symmetric charge distribution around its centre. The electric field contributions from diametrically opposite elements of the ring are equal in magnitude but exactly opposite in direction. Therefore, when integrated over the entire ring, the net electric field at the centre cancels out completely and equals zero. Options A, C, and D incorrectly suggest a non-zero field, which would only arise for asymmetric charge distributions.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) शून्य है। एकसमान आवेशित वृत्ताकार वलय में आवेश वितरण सममित होता है। वलय के व्यासीय रूप से विपरीत तत्वों के विद्युत-क्षेत्र का योगदान परिमाण में समान परंतु दिशा में विपरीत होता है, अतः केंद्र पर नेट विद्युत-क्षेत्र शून्य होता है।
questions.topic: Electric field due to uniformly charged ring

questions.text: त्रिज्या r के किसी आवेशित गोले का पृष्ठीय आवेश घनत्व σ है। इसके पृष्ठ पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र E है। यदि आवेश घनत्व समान रखते हुए गोले की त्रिज्या दुगुनी कर दी जाए, तो पुराने गोले और नए गोले के विद्युत-क्षेत्रों का अनुपात होगा:
questions.text_english: A charged sphere of radius r has surface charge density σ. The electric field on its surface is E. If the radius of the sphere is doubled, keeping charge density the same, the ratio of the electric field on the old sphere to that on the new sphere will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1. The electric field at the surface of a uniformly charged sphere is given by E = σ/ε₀, which depends only on the surface charge density σ and not on the radius of the sphere. Since the surface charge density is kept the same when the radius is doubled, the electric field on both the old and the new sphere remains identical. Hence their ratio is 1:1 = 1. Options B, C, and D are incorrect as they wrongly assume the field depends on the radius.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) 1 है। किसी आवेशित गोले के पृष्ठ पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र E = σ/ε₀ होता है, जो केवल पृष्ठीय आवेश घनत्व पर निर्भर करता है, त्रिज्या पर नहीं। चूँकि σ समान रखा गया है, दोनों गोलों के पृष्ठ पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र समान होगा और उनका अनुपात 1 होगा।
questions.topic: Electric field at surface of charged sphere

questions.text: किसी छात्र से चार सेलों, जिनमें प्रत्येक का वि.वा. बल (emf) E तथा आंतरिक प्रतिरोध r है, को श्रेणी में संयोजित करने के लिए कहा गया है। परंतु वह इनमें से एक सेल को अन्य सेलों के साथ गलत ढंग से श्रेणी में संयोजित करता/करती है। संयोजन के तुल्य वि.वा. बल (emf) और तुल्य आंतरिक प्रतिरोध होंगे क्रमशः:
questions.text_english: A student is asked to connect four cells, each of emf E and internal resistance r, in series. But she/he connects one cell wrongly in series with the other cells. The equivalent emf and the equivalent internal resistance of the combination will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 2E and 4r. When one cell is connected in reverse, its emf opposes the other three. The net equivalent emf = 3E − E = 2E. The internal resistances of all four cells always add up in series regardless of orientation, so equivalent internal resistance = 4r. Options A and B suggest an emf of 4E which is only possible when all cells aid each other. Option C gives 3E which incorrectly handles the resistance.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) 2E और 4r है। जब एक सेल विपरीत दिशा में जोड़ा जाता है, तो तुल्य emf = 3E − E = 2E होगा। आंतरिक प्रतिरोध सभी सेलों के श्रेणी में जोड़ने पर = 4r होगा।
questions.topic: Cells in series with one reversed

questions.text: तार को मोड़कर वृत्ताकार पाश A के रूप में बनाया गया है जिसमें I धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। तार को फिर दो फेरों के वृत्ताकार पाश B में मोड़ा गया और उसी धारा को प्रवाहित किया गया। पाश A और पाश B के केंद्रों पर चुंबकीय क्षेत्रों का अनुपात होगा:
questions.text_english: A piece of wire bent in the form of a circular loop A carries a current I. The wire is then bent into a circular loop B of two turns and carries the same current. The ratio of magnetic fields at the centre of loop A to that of loop B will be:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1/16. When the wire is bent into two turns, the total length of wire remains constant. If loop A has radius R, then loop B (with 2 turns) has radius R/2. The magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop is B = μ₀nI/(2r). For loop A: B_A = μ₀I/(2R). For loop B: B_B = μ₀(2)I/(2 × R/2) = 2μ₀I/R. Therefore, B_A/B_B = [μ₀I/(2R)] / [2μ₀I/R] = 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) 1/16 है। तार की कुल लंबाई स्थिर रहती है। यदि पाश A की त्रिज्या R है, तो पाश B की त्रिज्या R/2 होगी। B_A/B_B = (μ₀I/2R) / (2μ₀I/R) = 1/16।
questions.topic: Magnetic field at centre of circular loop

questions.text: कोई 10 cm लंबा तार y-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है। इससे धनात्मक y-दिशा में 1.0 A की धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस क्षेत्र में कोई चुंबकीय क्षेत्र B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂ विद्यमान है। इस तार पर बल है:
questions.text_english: A 10 cm long wire lies along y-axis. It carries a current of 1.0 A in positive y-direction. A magnetic field B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂ exists in the region. The force on the wire is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (0.8 mN)î. The force on the wire is F = IL × B. Here, L = 0.1 ĵ m, I = 1.0 A, B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂. F = 1.0 × [0.1 ĵ × (0.005 ĵ + 0.008 k̂)] = 0.1 × [0.005(ĵ × ĵ) + 0.008(ĵ × k̂)] = 0.1 × [0 + 0.008 î] = 0.0008 î N = 0.8 mN î. The ĵ × ĵ = 0 and ĵ × k̂ = î, so only the k̂ component of B contributes to the force.
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in magnetic field

questions.text: प्रतिरोध G के किसी गैल्वेनोमीटर को 0 से I A परिसर के एमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है। यदि इस गैल्वेनोमीटर में प्रवाहित धारा I A की 0·1% है, तो एमीटर का प्रतिरोध है:
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance G is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I A. If the current through the galvanometer is 0.1% of I A, the resistance of the ammeter is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) G/999. The galvanometer carries 0.1% of I, i.e., I_g = 0.001I. The shunt current = I − 0.001I = 0.999I. By condition of parallel combination: I_g × G = (I − I_g) × S, so S = (0.001I × G)/(0.999I) = G/999. The equivalent resistance of ammeter = GS/(G+S) ≈ S = G/999, since S << G. Option B (G/1000) is a common approximation but not exact.
questions.topic: Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter

questions.text: कोई चालक वृत्ताकार पाश किसी एकसमान चुंबकीय क्षेत्र B = 50 mT में चुंबकीय क्षेत्र के समतल लंबवत् स्थित है। पाश की त्रिज्या 1 mm s⁻¹ की एकसमान दर से सिकुड़ रही है। जिस क्षण पाश की त्रिज्या 4 cm है, तब पाश में प्रेरित वि.वा. बल (emf) है:
questions.text_english: A conducting circular loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field B = 50 mT with its plane perpendicular to the magnetic field. The radius of the loop is made to shrink at a constant rate of 1 mm s⁻¹. At the instant the radius of the loop is 4 cm, the induced emf in the loop is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 4π μV. The induced emf is |ε| = dΦ/dt = B × d(πr²)/dt = B × 2πr × (dr/dt). Here B = 50 × 10⁻³ T, r = 4 × 10⁻² m, dr/dt = −1 × 10⁻³ m/s (shrinking). |ε| = 50 × 10⁻³ × 2π × 4 × 10⁻² × 1 × 10⁻³ = 50 × 2π × 4 × 10⁻⁸ = 4π × 10⁻⁶ V = 4π μV.
questions.topic: Induced emf in shrinking loop

questions.text: किसी विद्युत-चुंबकीय तरंग के विद्युत और चुंबकीय क्षेत्र:
questions.text_english: The electric and magnetic fields of electromagnetic waves are:

options.A: एक-दूसरे के लंबवत् और समान कला में होते हैं।
options.B: एक-दूसरे के लंबवत् नहीं होते और समान कला में होते हैं।
options.C: एक-दूसरे के लंबवत् होते हैं लेकिन समान कला में नहीं होते हैं।
options.D: न तो एक-दूसरे के लंबवत् और न ही समान कला में होते हैं।

options_english.A: In the same phase and perpendicular to each other.
options_english.B: In the same phase and not perpendicular to each other.
options_english.C: Not in the same phase but are perpendicular to each other.
options_english.D: Neither in the same phase nor perpendicular to each other.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) In the same phase and perpendicular to each other. In an electromagnetic wave, the electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) oscillate in phase with each other, meaning they reach their maximum and minimum values simultaneously. They are also mutually perpendicular to each other and to the direction of wave propagation. This is a fundamental property of transverse electromagnetic waves established by Maxwell's equations.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। विद्युत-चुंबकीय तरंग में विद्युत क्षेत्र (E) और चुंबकीय क्षेत्र (B) समान कला में होते हैं और एक-दूसरे के लंबवत् होते हैं तथा तरंग की संचरण दिशा के भी लंबवत् होते हैं।
questions.topic: Properties of electromagnetic waves

questions.text: दो पुंज, A और B जिनके फ़ोटॉनों की ऊर्जा क्रमशः 3·3 eV और 11·3 eV हैं, क्रमवार किसी धात्विक पृष्ठ (कार्य-फलन 2·3 eV) को प्रदीप्त करते हैं। पुंज A के कारण उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम चाल का पुंज B से अनुपात होगा:
questions.text_english: Two beams, A and B whose photon energies are 3·3 eV and 11·3 eV respectively, illuminate a metallic surface (work function 2·3 eV) successively. The ratio of maximum speed of electrons emitted due to beam A to that due to beam B is:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1/3. Using the photoelectric equation: KE = hν − φ. For beam A: KE_A = 3.3 − 2.3 = 1.0 eV. For beam B: KE_B = 11.3 − 2.3 = 9.0 eV. Since KE = ½mv², we have v ∝ √(KE). Therefore, v_A/v_B = √(KE_A/KE_B) = √(1.0/9.0) = 1/3. So the ratio of maximum speeds is 1/3.
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect - maximum speed of emitted electrons

questions.text: किसी गतिमान इलेक्ट्रॉन और किसी गतिमान प्रोटॉन से संबद्ध तरंगों का तरंगदैर्घ्य समान λ है। इसका यह अभिप्राय है कि इनका/इनकी समान है:
questions.text_english: The waves associated with a moving electron and a moving proton have the same wavelength λ. It implies that they have the same:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) momentum. According to de Broglie's relation, λ = h/p, where h is Planck's constant and p is the momentum. If two particles have the same de Broglie wavelength λ, then p = h/λ is the same for both. Since the electron and proton have different masses, they would have different speeds and different kinetic energies for the same momentum. Therefore, only momentum is identical.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) संवेग है। de Broglie संबंध λ = h/p के अनुसार, यदि तरंगदैर्घ्य समान है, तो संवेग p = h/λ भी समान होगा। द्रव्यमान अलग-अलग होने के कारण चाल और ऊर्जा अलग होंगी।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength

questions.text: Ge का मादन As के साथ किया गया है। इसके कारण:
questions.text_english: Ge is doped with As. Due to doping,

options.A: Ge के जालक की संरचना विकृत हो जाती है।
options.B: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.C: होलों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.D: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में कमी होती है।

options_english.A: the structure of Ge lattice is distorted.
options_english.B: the number of conduction electrons increases.
options_english.D: the number of conduction electrons decreases.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) the number of conduction electrons increases. Arsenic (As) is a pentavalent (group 15) element. When it is used to dope Germanium (a tetravalent semiconductor), four of its five valence electrons form covalent bonds with neighbouring Ge atoms, while the fifth electron becomes a free conduction electron. This creates an n-type semiconductor with an increased number of conduction electrons. Holes are minority carriers in this case.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। आर्सेनिक (As) पंचसंयोजी तत्व है। Ge में मादन से इसका पाँचवाँ इलेक्ट्रॉन मुक्त हो जाता है और चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या बढ़ जाती है। यह n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक बनाता है।
questions.topic: n-type semiconductor doping

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के स्पेक्ट्रम में बामर श्रेणी की दूसरी स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखा के निर्माण के लिए उत्तरदायी इलेक्ट्रॉन का संक्रमण किसके संगत है?
questions.text_english: The transition of electron that gives rise to the formation of the second spectral line of the Balmer series in the spectrum of hydrogen atom corresponds to:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) nf = 2 and ni = 4. The Balmer series corresponds to all transitions ending at nf = 2. The first line (Hα) is the transition from ni = 3 to nf = 2, and the second line (Hβ) is from ni = 4 to nf = 2. Therefore the second spectral line of the Balmer series corresponds to the transition from ni = 4 to nf = 2.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) nf = 2 और ni = 4 है। बामर श्रेणी में सभी संक्रमण nf = 2 पर समाप्त होते हैं। पहली रेखा ni = 3 से और दूसरी रेखा ni = 4 से होती है।
questions.topic: Hydrogen spectrum - Balmer series

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : समतल दर्पण और उत्तल दर्पण किसी भी परिस्थिति में वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब नहीं बना सकते हैं।
कारण (R) : कोई आभासी प्रतिबिंब वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब बनाने के लिए बिंब की भांति कार्य नहीं कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Plane and convex mirrors cannot produce real images under any circumstance.
Reason (R) : A virtual image cannot serve as an object to produce a real image.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों वक्तव्य दिए गए हैं। नीचे दिए गए कूट (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. Assertion (A) is true: plane and convex mirrors always form virtual, erect images for real objects and cannot independently produce real images. However, Reason (R) is false because a virtual image CAN serve as a virtual object for another optical element (like a converging lens or concave mirror placed in the path) to produce a real image. Thus R does not correctly explain A, and moreover R itself is incorrect as a general statement.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। अभिकथन (A) सत्य है — समतल और उत्तल दर्पण वास्तविक प्रतिबिंब नहीं बना सकते। परंतु कारण (R) असत्य है क्योंकि आभासी प्रतिबिंब एक अन्य प्रकाशीय तत्व के लिए आभासी बिंब का कार्य कर सकता है।
questions.topic: Image formation by plane and convex mirror

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी बैटरी से श्रेणी में संयोजित और स्वतंत्रतापूर्वक निलंबित दो लंबे समांतर तार एक-दूसरे से दूर हटते हैं।
कारण (R) : विपरीत दिशाओं में प्रवाहित धारावाही दो तार एक-दूसरे को प्रतिकर्षित करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Two long parallel wires, freely suspended and connected in series to a battery, move apart.
Reason (R) : Two wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों वक्तव्य दिए गए हैं। नीचे दिए गए कूट में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Select the correct answer.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।

questions.text: आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार दो बैटरियाँ जिनके वि.वा. बल (emf) 6 V और 3 V हैं तथा आंतरिक प्रतिरोध क्रमशः 0·8 Ω और 0·2 Ω हैं, किसी बाह्य प्रतिरोध R से श्रेणी में संयोजित हैं। R का वह मान ज्ञात कीजिए ताकि 6 V की बैटरी के सिरों पर विभवांतर शून्य हो।
questions.text_english: Two batteries of emfs 6 V and 3 V and internal resistances 0·8 Ω and 0·2 Ω respectively are connected in series to an external resistance R, as shown in figure. Find the value of R so that the potential difference across the 6 V battery be zero.

key_points: R = 1 Ω
Setting up the condition V_6V = 0 means 6 − I × 0.8 = 0, giving I = 7.5 A
Total EMF = 6 + 3 = 9 V, total resistance = 0.8 + 0.2 + R, current I = 9/(1 + R)
Setting I = 7.5 A: 9/(1 + R) = 7.5, giving R = 0.2 Ω

questions.solution: For the potential difference across the 6 V battery to be zero, we apply Kirchhoff's voltage law across that battery: V = E₁ − I × r₁ = 0, so 6 − I × 0.8 = 0, giving I = 7.5 A. Both batteries are aiding (in same direction), so total emf = 6 + 3 = 9 V and total resistance = r₁ + r₂ + R = 0.8 + 0.2 + R = 1 + R. Using I = Total EMF / Total resistance: 7.5 = 9 / (1 + R), so 1 + R = 1.2, therefore R = 0.2 Ω.
questions.solution_hindi: 6 V बैटरी के सिरों पर विभवांतर शून्य होने के लिए: 6 − I × 0.8 = 0 → I = 7.5 A। कुल emf = 9 V, कुल प्रतिरोध = 1 + R। 7.5 = 9/(1 + R) → R = 0.2 Ω।

questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा E के किसी न्यूट्रॉन (द्रव्यमान m) तथा समान ऊर्जा के किसी फ़ोटॉन पर विचार कीजिए। मान लीजिए न्यूट्रॉन की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्घ्य λn तथा फ़ोटॉन की तरंगदैर्घ्य λp है। λn/λp के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Consider a neutron (mass m) of kinetic energy E and a photon of the same energy. Let λn and λp be the de Broglie wavelength of neutron and the wavelength of photon respectively. Obtain an expression for λn/λp.

key_points: λn/λp = √(E / 2mc²)
For neutron: λn = h/p = h/√(2mE)
For photon: λp = hc/E
Ratio: λn/λp = [h/√(2mE)] / [hc/E] = E / (c√(2mE)) = √(E/2mc²)

questions.solution: For the neutron with kinetic energy E: the momentum p = √(2mE), so the de Broglie wavelength is λn = h/p = h/√(2mE). For the photon with energy E: E = hc/λp, so λp = hc/E. Therefore the ratio is λn/λp = [h/√(2mE)] / [hc/E] = [h × E] / [hc × √(2mE)] = E / [c√(2mE)] = √(E/2mc²). Thus λn/λp = √(E/2mc²).
questions.solution_hindi: न्यूट्रॉन के लिए: λn = h/√(2mE)। फ़ोटॉन के लिए: λp = hc/E। अतः λn/λp = E/(c√(2mE)) = √(E/2mc²)।

questions.text_english:
(a) Monochromatic light of frequency 5·0 × 10¹⁴ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index 1·5. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.
OR
(b) A plano-convex lens of focal length 16 cm is made of a material of refractive index 1.4. Calculate the radius of the curved surface of the lens.

key_points: (a)(i) Reflected wavelength = 6 × 10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm (same as incident, stays in air)
(a)(ii) Refracted wavelength = 4 × 10⁻⁷ m = 400 nm (wavelength in medium = λ/n)
(b) Using lensmaker's equation for plano-convex lens: 1/f = (n−1)[1/R1 − 1/R2], R = 6.4 cm

questions.solution:
Part (a): The wavelength in air = c/f = (3 × 10⁸)/(5 × 10¹⁴) = 6 × 10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm. (i) The reflected ray remains in air, so its wavelength is unchanged = 600 nm. (ii) The refracted ray travels in the medium of refractive index 1.5. The frequency remains constant, so the wavelength in the medium = λ_air/n = 600/1.5 = 400 nm.

Part (b): For a plano-convex lens, one surface is flat (R₂ = ∞) and one is curved (R₁ = R). Using the lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n − 1)[1/R₁ − 1/R₂] = (1.4 − 1)[1/R − 0] = 0.4/R. Given f = 16 cm: 1/16 = 0.4/R, so R = 0.4 × 16 = 6.4 cm.

questions.text: कोई बिंब 40 cm वक्रता त्रिज्या के किसी अवतल दर्पण के सामने 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। (i) बने प्रतिबिंब की स्थिति तथा (ii) प्रतिबिंब का आवर्धन ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm. Find the (i) position of the image formed and (ii) magnification of the image.

key_points: Focal length f = R/2 = −20 cm (concave mirror)
Using mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; u = −30 cm
1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/20 + 1/30 = −1/60; v = −60 cm (real, in front of mirror)
Magnification m = −v/u = −(−60)/(−30) = −2 (real, inverted, magnified)

questions.solution: The radius of curvature R = 40 cm, so focal length f = −R/2 = −20 cm (negative for concave mirror). Object distance u = −30 cm. Using the mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, we get 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/(−20) − 1/(−30) = −1/20 + 1/30 = (−3 + 2)/60 = −1/60. Therefore v = −60 cm. The image is formed 60 cm in front of the mirror (real and inverted). Magnification m = −v/u = −(−60)/(−30) = −2. The image is real, inverted, and twice the size of the object.
questions.solution_hindi: f = −20 cm, u = −30 cm। दर्पण सूत्र से: 1/v = 1/(−20) − 1/(−30) = −1/60 → v = −60 cm। प्रतिबिंब दर्पण के सामने 60 cm पर, वास्तविक और उल्टा। आवर्धन m = −v/u = −2।

questions.text: किसी नैज अर्धचालक की चालकता ताप के साथ किस प्रकार परिवर्तित होती है? व्याख्या कीजिए। विचरण को ग्राफ द्वारा दर्शाइए।
questions.text_english: How does the conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor vary with temperature? Explain. Show the variation in a plot.

key_points: Conductivity of intrinsic semiconductor increases with increase in temperature
At higher temperature, more electron-hole pairs are generated due to thermal excitation across the band gap
The graph shows an exponential increase of conductivity with temperature

questions.solution: The conductivity of an intrinsic semiconductor increases exponentially with increase in temperature. At absolute zero, all electrons are in the valence band and conductivity is zero. As temperature increases, thermal energy excites electrons from the valence band across the energy gap into the conduction band, generating electron-hole pairs. Both electrons and holes act as charge carriers, increasing conductivity. The graph shows an exponential rise: σ increases steeply as T increases, because the number of thermally generated carriers grows exponentially with temperature.
questions.solution_hindi: नैज अर्धचालक की चालकता ताप के साथ चरघातांकी रूप से बढ़ती है। ताप बढ़ने पर अधिक इलेक्ट्रॉन-होल युगल उत्पन्न होते हैं जिससे आवेश वाहकों की संख्या और चालकता बढ़ती है। ग्राफ में σ बनाम T एक चरघातांकी वक्र होता है।

questions.text: तीन बिंदु आवेश Q₁, Q₂ तथा Q₃, x−y तल में क्रमशः बिंदुओं (−d, 0), (0, 0) और (d, 0) पर स्थित हैं। Q₁ और Q₃ समरूप हैं तथा Q₂ धनात्मक है। आवेश Q₁ की प्रकृति और मान क्या हों ताकि इन आवेशों के निकाय की स्थितिज ऊर्जा शून्य हो?
questions.text_english: Three point charges Q₁, Q₂ and Q₃ are located in x−y plane at points (−d, 0), (0, 0) and (d, 0) respectively. Q₁ and Q₃ are identical and Q₂ is positive. What will be the nature and value of Q₁ so that the potential energy of the system is zero?

key_points: Q₁ must be negative
Total PE = k[Q₁Q₂/d + Q₂Q₃/d + Q₁Q₃/2d] = 0
Since Q₁ = Q₃ = Q: k/d [QQ₂ + Q₂Q + Q²/2] = 0 → 2QQ₂ + Q²/2 = 0
Q = −4Q₂

questions.solution: Let Q₁ = Q₃ = Q and Q₂ be positive. The distances are: between Q₁ and Q₂ = d, between Q₂ and Q₃ = d, and between Q₁ and Q₃ = 2d. The total potential energy of the system is U = k[Q₁Q₂/d + Q₂Q₃/d + Q₁Q₃/2d] = k/d [QQ₂ + Q₂Q + Q²/2] = k/d [2QQ₂ + Q²/2]. Setting U = 0: 2QQ₂ + Q²/2 = 0, which gives 2Q₂ = −Q/2, so Q = −4Q₂. Therefore Q₁ must be negative and its magnitude is 4Q₂. Q₁ = Q₃ = −4Q₂.
questions.solution_hindi: माना Q₁ = Q₃ = Q। दूरियाँ: Q₁−Q₂ = d, Q₂−Q₃ = d, Q₁−Q₃ = 2d। कुल स्थितिज ऊर्जा U = k/d[2QQ₂ + Q²/2] = 0 → Q = −4Q₂। अतः Q₁ ऋणात्मक होना चाहिए और Q₁ = −4Q₂।

अथवा
(ख) व्हीटस्टोन सेतु किसे कहते हैं? व्हीटस्टोन सेतु के संतुलन के लिए आवश्यक शर्तें प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Define 'current density'. Is it a scalar or a vector? An electric field E is maintained in a metallic conductor. If n be the number of electrons (mass m, charge −e) per unit volume in the conductor and τ its relaxation time, show that the current density j = αE, where α = (ne²/m)τ.
OR
(b) What is a Wheatstone bridge? Obtain the necessary conditions under which the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

key_points: (a) Current density j = I/A (current per unit area perpendicular to flow); it is a vector quantity
Drift velocity v_d = eEτ/m (from force on electron and relaxation time)
Current I = nAev_d; j = I/A = nev_d = ne(eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m)E = αE where α = ne²τ/m
(b) Wheatstone bridge is a circuit with four resistances P, Q, R, S; balanced condition is P/Q = R/S (no current through galvanometer)

questions.solution:
Part (a): Current density is defined as the electric current flowing per unit cross-sectional area perpendicular to the direction of flow. It is a vector quantity directed along the direction of current. When an electric field E is applied, each electron experiences a force F = eE, which gives it an acceleration a = eE/m. During the relaxation time τ, the drift velocity acquired is v_d = aτ = eEτ/m. The current density j = nev_d = ne × (eEτ/m) = (ne²τ/m) × E = αE, where α = ne²τ/m. This proves the required relation.

Part (b): A Wheatstone bridge consists of four resistances P, Q, R, and S arranged in a quadrilateral with a battery across one diagonal and a galvanometer across the other. The bridge is balanced when no current flows through the galvanometer. Applying Kirchhoff's laws at balance: the potential at junctions B and D must be equal. This gives the balanced condition P/Q = R/S, or equivalently PS = QR.

questions.text_english:
A bar magnet of magnetic moment 2·5 JT⁻¹ lies aligned with the direction of a uniform magnetic field of 0·32 T.
(a) Find the amount of work done to turn the magnet so as to align its magnetic moment (i) normal to the field direction, and (ii) opposite to the field direction.
(b) What is the torque on the magnet in above cases (i) and (ii)?

key_points: Work done W = MB(cosθ₁ − cosθ₂); initial angle θ₁ = 0°
(b)(i) τ = MB sin90° = 0.8 N·m; (b)(ii) τ = MB sin180° = 0 N·m

questions.solution:
Given: M = 2.5 JT⁻¹, B = 0.32 T. Initially the magnet is aligned with the field, so θ₁ = 0°. The work done is W = MB(cosθ₁ − cosθ₂).

Part (a)(i): θ₂ = 90°, W = 2.5 × 0.32 × (cos0° − cos90°) = 0.8 × (1 − 0) = 0.8 J.

Part (a)(ii): θ₂ = 180°, W = 2.5 × 0.32 × (cos0° − cos180°) = 0.8 × (1 − (−1)) = 0.8 × 2 = 1.6 J.

Part (b)(i): At θ = 90°, torque τ = MB sinθ = 2.5 × 0.32 × sin90° = 0.8 × 1 = 0.8 N·m.

Part (b)(ii): At θ = 180°, torque τ = MB sin180° = 2.5 × 0.32 × 0 = 0 N·m.

questions.text_english:
Consider the arrangement of two coils P and Q shown in the figure. When current in coil P is switched on or switched off, a current flows in coil Q.
(a) Explain the phenomenon involved in it.
(b) Mention two factors on which the current produced in coil Q depends.
(c) Give the direction of current in coil Q when there is a current in the coil P and (i) R is increased, and (ii) R is decreased.

key_points: (a) Mutual induction: changing current in P changes magnetic flux through Q, inducing an emf and current in Q
(b) Rate of change of current in P; coefficient of mutual inductance between the coils
(c)(i) R increases → current in P decreases → flux through Q decreases → induced current in Q in same sense as current in P (to oppose decrease by Lenz's law)
(c)(ii) R decreases → current in P increases → flux through Q increases → induced current in Q in opposite sense to current in P

questions.solution:
Part (a): The phenomenon is mutual induction. When the current in coil P changes (switched on or off), the magnetic flux linked with coil Q changes. According to Faraday's law, this changing flux induces an emf in coil Q, which drives a current through it. This is mutual electromagnetic induction.

Part (b): The induced current in coil Q depends on (1) the rate of change of current in coil P (dI_P/dt), and (2) the mutual inductance M between the two coils, which itself depends on the geometry and closeness of the coils.

Part (c): (i) When R is increased, current in P decreases, so flux through Q decreases. By Lenz's law, the induced current in Q will flow in such a direction as to oppose this decrease, i.e., in the same direction as current in P. (ii) When R is decreased, current in P increases, so flux through Q increases. The induced current in Q will oppose this increase and flow in the direction opposite to current in P.
questions.solution_hindi: (a) अन्योन्य प्रेरण — P की बदलती धारा Q में फ्लक्स परिवर्तन करती है जिससे Q में प्रेरित emf उत्पन्न होती है। (b) P में धारा परिवर्तन की दर; कुंडलियों के बीच अन्योन्य प्रेरकत्व। (c)(i) R बढ़ने पर Q में धारा P की धारा के समान दिशा में। (ii) R घटने पर Q में धारा P की धारा के विपरीत दिशा में।

questions.text: रदरफोर्ड के परमाणु मॉडल की कमियाँ लिखिए। बोर ने उन्हें किस प्रकार दूर किया? यह दर्शाइए कि बोर परमाणु की विभिन्न कक्षाओं के बीच की दूरियाँ समान नहीं होती हैं।
questions.text_english: Write the drawbacks of Rutherford's atomic model. How did Bohr remove them? Show that the distances between the different orbits of the Bohr atom are not equal.

key_points: Drawback 1: Rutherford's model predicted that orbiting electrons continuously emit radiation and spiral into nucleus (unstable atom)
Drawback 2: Could not explain the discrete line spectra of hydrogen
Bohr postulated stationary orbits with quantised angular momentum: mvr = nh/2π; electrons do not radiate in these orbits
Bohr explained radiation only when electrons jump between orbits: hν = E_i − E_f
Radius r_n = n²a₀; differences r_(n+1) − r_n = (2n+1)a₀ increase with n, so orbits are not equally spaced

questions.solution:
Rutherford's model had two major drawbacks. First, according to classical electrodynamics, an accelerating electron (moving in a circular orbit) must continuously radiate electromagnetic energy. As it loses energy, it would spiral inward and collapse into the nucleus, making the atom unstable — but atoms are stable. Second, the model could not explain the discrete line spectrum observed for hydrogen; it predicted a continuous spectrum.

Bohr removed these drawbacks by proposing two postulates: (i) electrons revolve only in certain allowed stationary orbits where angular momentum is quantised as mvr = nh/2π, and in these orbits they do not radiate; (ii) energy is emitted or absorbed only when an electron jumps between two orbits: hν = E_i − E_f.

To show orbits are unequally spaced: the radius of the n-th orbit is r_n = n²a₀, where a₀ = 0.529 Å. The separation between orbits n and (n+1) is r_{n+1} − r_n = [(n+1)² − n²]a₀ = (2n+1)a₀. Since this increases with n, the orbits are NOT equally spaced — they become farther apart for higher orbits.
questions.solution_hindi: रदरफोर्ड की कमियाँ: (1) त्वरित इलेक्ट्रॉन को विकिरण उत्सर्जित करके नाभिक में गिरना चाहिए। (2) हाइड्रोजन के रेखा स्पेक्ट्रम की व्याख्या नहीं। बोर ने: (i) mvr = nh/2π के साथ स्थायी कक्षाएँ प्रस्तावित कीं जिनमें विकिरण नहीं। (ii) कक्षाओं के बीच संक्रमण से hν = E_i − E_f। r_n = n²a₀; r_{n+1} − r_n = (2n+1)a₀ जो n के साथ बढ़ता है, अतः कक्षाएँ समान दूरी पर नहीं।

questions.text_english:
(a) The wavelength of an electromagnetic wave is often related to the characteristic size of the system that generates it. Give two examples to justify this statement.
(b) (i) Long distance radio broadcasts use short-wave bands. Why?
(ii) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground, but X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why?

key_points: (a) Example 1: Nuclear gamma rays have wavelength ~10⁻¹² m, comparable to nuclear size (~10⁻¹⁵ m)
(a) Example 2: Microwave ovens use ~cm wavelengths comparable to size of molecules/cavities
(b)(i) Short waves are reflected by the ionosphere, allowing long-distance broadcasting without line-of-sight
(b)(ii) X-rays are absorbed by Earth's atmosphere; satellites above the atmosphere can detect them

questions.solution:
Part (a): Two examples justifying the relation between wavelength and system size: (1) Atoms have a size of about 10⁻¹⁰ m, and they emit visible and ultraviolet light with wavelengths in the range 10⁻⁷ to 10⁻⁸ m — of the same order. (2) Nuclei have a size of about 10⁻¹⁵ m, and they emit gamma rays with wavelengths around 10⁻¹² m — again of the same order of magnitude as the emitting system.

Part (b)(i): Short-wave bands (wavelength ~10–100 m) are reflected by the ionosphere back to Earth. This allows them to travel large distances around the curvature of the Earth without any relay stations, making them ideal for long-distance radio broadcasts.

Part (b)(ii): Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays completely, so X-ray telescopes placed on the ground receive no signal from celestial sources. Only satellites orbiting above the atmosphere can detect incoming X-rays from astronomical objects. Optical and radio waves, however, pass through the atmosphere, so optical and radio telescopes work effectively on the ground.

questions.text_english:
(a) Write two characteristic properties of nuclear force.
(b) Draw a plot of potential energy of a pair of nucleons as a function of their separation. Write two important conclusions that can be drawn from the plot.

key_points: (a) Nuclear force is short-range (acts only up to ~1 fm) and is charge-independent (same between p-p, n-n, p-n)
(a) Nuclear force is the strongest known force and is attractive for distances > 0.8 fm but repulsive for < 0.8 fm
(b) Graph: PE is large positive (repulsive) for r < 0.8 fm, shows a deep minimum (~−100 MeV) at r ≈ 1 fm, then rises to zero for large r
Conclusions: (1) Nuclear force has a short range and is attractive around 1 fm; (2) Below 0.8 fm it becomes strongly repulsive (hard core repulsion) preventing nuclear collapse

questions.solution:
Part (a): Two characteristic properties of nuclear force are: (1) Nuclear force is a short-range force — it is effective only over very small distances (up to about 2–3 fm) and falls to zero beyond that range. (2) Nuclear force is charge-independent — the force between two protons (p-p), two neutrons (n-n), and a proton-neutron (p-n) pair is approximately the same, which shows it does not depend on the electric charge of the nucleons.

Part (b): The potential energy versus separation graph shows a large positive (repulsive) value for r < 0.8 fm, a sharp minimum of about −100 MeV at r ≈ 1 fm (which is the equilibrium separation), then rises back towards zero for larger r, reaching zero by about 2–3 fm. Two conclusions: (1) The nuclear force is strongly attractive for separations around 1 fm, which is why nucleons are bound together inside the nucleus at this equilibrium distance. (2) For r < 0.8 fm, the potential energy rises sharply (hard core repulsion), which prevents nucleons from getting too close to each other and stabilises the nucleus.

questions.text_english:
Junction Diode as a Rectifier:
The process of conversion of an ac voltage into a dc voltage is called rectification and the device which performs this conversion is called a rectifier. The characteristics of a p-n junction diode reveal that when a p-n junction diode is forward biased, it offers a low resistance and when it is reverse biased, it offers a high resistance. Hence, a p-n junction diode conducts only when it is forward biased. This property of a p-n junction diode makes it suitable for its use as a rectifier. Thus, when an ac voltage is applied across a p-n junction, it conducts only during those alternate half cycles for which it is forward biased. A rectifier which rectifies only half cycle of an ac voltage is called a half-wave rectifier and one that rectifies both the half cycles is known as a full-wave rectifier.

sub_questions.text_english: The root mean square value of an alternating voltage applied to a full-wave rectifier is V₀/√2. Then the root mean square value of the rectified output voltage is:
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) V₀/√2. In a full-wave rectifier, the output is always positive (both half-cycles are rectified). The rms value of the rectified full-wave output is the same as the rms value of the original ac input because rectification does not change the magnitude of the waveform — it only flips the negative half positive. Therefore, rms of output = V₀/√2, same as the input rms.

sub_questions.text: किसी पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी में प्रत्येक डायोड से धारा प्रवाहित होती है:
sub_questions.text_english: In a full-wave rectifier, the current in each of the diodes flows for:

options.A: निवेश सिग्नल के पूर्ण चक्र के लिए
options.B: निवेश सिग्नल के अर्ध-चक्र के लिए

options.D: निवेश सिग्नल के केवल धनात्मक अर्ध-चक्र के लिए

options_english.A: Complete cycle of the input signal
options_english.B: Half cycle of the input signal
options_english.C: Less than half cycle of the input signal
options_english.D: Only for the positive half cycle of the input signal

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Half cycle of the input signal. In a full-wave rectifier (centre-tap or bridge type), the two diodes conduct alternately. Each diode is forward biased only during one half-cycle of the input ac signal and is reverse biased during the other half-cycle. So each diode conducts for exactly one half-cycle of the input.

options.A: किसी निश्चित समय पर दोनों डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।
options.B: किसी निश्चित समय पर दोनों डायोड पश्चदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।
options.C: किसी निश्चित समय पर एक अग्रदिशिक बायसित तथा दूसरा पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है।
options.D: प्रथम अर्ध-चक्र में दोनों अग्रदिशिक बायसित होते हैं तथा द्वितीय अर्ध-चक्र में पश्चदिशिक बायसित होते हैं।

options_english.A: Both diodes are forward biased at the same time.
options_english.B: Both diodes are reverse biased at the same time.
options_english.C: One is forward biased and the other is reverse biased at the same time.
options_english.D: Both are forward biased in the first half of the cycle and reverse biased in the second half of the cycle.

sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). In a full-wave rectifier, the two diodes work in complementary fashion. At any given instant, the diode that is forward biased by the ac input conducts, while the other diode is reverse biased and does not conduct. They never both conduct or both block simultaneously. This alternating action ensures current always flows in the same direction through the load, giving full-wave rectification.

sub_questions.text: किसी काँच के बने उभयोत्तल लेंस के दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या R समान है तथा काँच का अपवर्तनांक n है। इस लेंस की क्षमता है:
sub_questions.text_english: A double-convex lens, with each face having same radius of curvature R, is made of glass of refractive index n. Its power is:
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 2(n−1)/R. For a double-convex lens with equal radii R, using the lensmaker's equation: 1/f = (n−1)[1/R₁ − 1/R₂] = (n−1)[1/R − (−1/R)] = (n−1) × 2/R = 2(n−1)/R. Therefore Power P = 1/f = 2(n−1)/R.

sub_questions.text: क्षमता P के किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस, जिसके दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या समान है, को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के लंबवत् दो समान भागों में काटा गया है। लेंस के एक भाग की क्षमता होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to its principal axis. The power of one part of the lens will be:
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) P/2. When a double-convex lens is cut perpendicular to its principal axis, each half becomes a plano-convex lens (one flat face and one curved face with radius R). For the original lens, P = 2(n−1)/R. For each half (plano-convex): P_half = (n−1)/R = P/2. So each part has power P/2.

sub_questions.text_english: The above two parts are kept in contact with each other as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be:
sub_questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) P. When the two plano-convex halves are placed in contact with their flat faces together (as shown in the figure, re-forming the original double-convex lens), the total power = P/2 + P/2 = P. questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A ray of light passes through a triangular prism. Show graphically, how the angle of deviation varies with the angle of incidence. Hence define the angle of minimum deviation.
(ii) A ray of light is incident normally on a refracting face of a prism of prism angle A and suffers a deviation of angle δ. Prove that the refractive index n of the material of the prism is given by n = sin(A + δ)/sin A.
(iii) The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2. If the refracting angle of the prism is 60°, find the: (1) Angle of minimum deviation, and (2) Angle of incidence.
OR
(b) (i) State Huygens' principle. A plane wavefront is incident at angle i on a reflecting surface. Construct the corresponding reflected wavefront. Using this diagram, prove that the angle of reflection is equal to the angle of incidence.
(ii) What are the coherent sources of light? Can two independent sodium lamps act like coherent sources? Explain.
(iii) A beam of light consisting of a known wavelength 520 nm and an unknown wavelength λ in Young's double-slit experiment produces two interference patterns such that the fourth bright fringe of unknown wavelength coincides with the fifth bright fringe of known wavelength. Find the value of λ.

key_points: (a)(i) Graph: deviation δ first decreases as i increases, reaches a minimum δ_m, then increases. At δ_m the ray passes symmetrically through the prism.
(a)(ii) When ray enters normal to first face, r₁ = 0, r₂ = A. By Snell's law at exit face: n sin A = sin(A+δ) → n = sin(A+δ)/sin A
(a)(iii) n = √2, A = 60°. At minimum deviation: n = sin((A+δ_m)/2)/sin(A/2) → √2 = sin((60+δ_m)/2)/sin30° → δ_m = 30°. Angle of incidence i = (A+δ_m)/2 = 45°

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): As the angle of incidence (i) increases from a small value, the angle of deviation (δ) first decreases, reaches a minimum value called the angle of minimum deviation (δ_m), and then increases. At minimum deviation, the ray travels symmetrically through the prism, parallel to the base. The angle of minimum deviation δ_m is defined as the angle of deviation at which the deviation is minimum, occurring when the ray passes symmetrically through the prism (i.e., the angle of refraction at the first surface equals the angle of incidence at the second surface).

Part (a)(ii): When the ray is incident normally on the first refracting face, angle of incidence at first face = 0, so angle of refraction at first face r₁ = 0. Since r₁ + r₂ = A (for a prism), r₂ = A. At the second face, applying Snell's law: n sin(r₂) = 1 × sin(angle of emergence). The angle of deviation δ = angle of emergence − r₂ (since ray bends at exit face only). So angle of emergence = A + δ. Snell's law gives: n sin A = sin(A + δ), therefore n = sin(A + δ)/sin A.

Part (a)(iii): For minimum deviation with n = √2, A = 60°: n = sin((A + δ_m)/2) / sin(A/2). √2 = sin((60° + δ_m)/2) / sin 30° = sin((60° + δ_m)/2) / 0.5. So sin((60° + δ_m)/2) = √2/2 = sin 45°. Thus (60° + δ_m)/2 = 45° → δ_m = 30°. The angle of incidence i = (A + δ_m)/2 = (60° + 30°)/2 = 45°.

Part (b)(i): Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets that spread out in the forward direction with the speed of light in that medium. The new wavefront at a later time is the envelope (common tangent) to all these secondary wavelets. For the proof of the law of reflection: draw the incident wavefront AB striking the reflecting surface. While the secondary wavelet from A travels a distance vt to reach A', the wavelet from B travels the same distance to reach B'. The reflected wavefront A'B' is tangent to all secondary wavelets. Since the two triangles (formed by the incident and reflected wavefronts with the reflecting surface) are congruent (same hypotenuse and equal sides vt), the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

Part (b)(ii): Coherent sources are sources of light that emit light of the same frequency (or wavelength) and maintain a constant phase difference. Two independent sodium lamps cannot act as coherent sources because, although they emit light of the same wavelength, the phase of emission from individual atoms changes randomly and independently at very short intervals (~10⁻⁸ s). There is no fixed phase relationship between the two lamps, so no stable interference pattern is produced.

Part (b)(iii): The position of the n-th bright fringe is yn = nλD/d. For the fourth bright fringe of λ to coincide with the fifth bright fringe of 520 nm: 4λ = 5 × 520 nm → λ = (5 × 520)/4 = 650 nm.
questions.solution_hindi: (a)(i) i बढ़ने पर δ पहले घटता है, δ_m पर न्यूनतम होता है, फिर बढ़ता है। (a)(ii) n = sin(A+δ)/sinA। (a)(iii) δ_m = 30°, i = 45°। (b)(i) हाइगेन्स सिद्धांत: प्रत्येक बिंदु नए तरंगाग्र का स्रोत है। (b)(ii) दो स्वतंत्र Na लैंप कला-संबद्ध नहीं होते। (b)(iii) 4λ = 5 × 520 → λ = 650 nm।

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Derive an expression for potential energy of an electric dipole p in an external uniform electric field E. When is the potential energy of the dipole (1) maximum, and (2) minimum?
(ii) An electric dipole consists of point charges −1·0 pC and +1·0 pC located at (0, 0) and (3 mm, 4 mm) respectively in x−y plane. An electric field E = 1000 V/m î is switched on in the region. Find the torque acting on the dipole.
OR
(b) (i) An electric dipole (dipole moment p = pî), consisting of charges −q and +q separated by distance 2a, is placed along the x-axis, with its centre at the origin. Show that the potential V, due to this dipole, at a point x, (x >> a) is equal to V = (1/4πε₀) × p/x².
(ii) Two isolated metallic spheres S₁ and S₂ of radii 1 cm and 3 cm respectively are charged such that both have the same charge density 10⁻² C/m². They are placed far away from each other and connected by a thin wire. Calculate the new charge on sphere S₁.

key_points: (a)(i) U = −p·E = −pE cosθ; max when θ = 180° (U = +pE); min when θ = 0° (U = −pE)
(a)(ii) Dipole length = √(3² + 4²) mm = 5 mm = 5 × 10⁻³ m; p = q × d = 1 × 10⁻¹² × 5 × 10⁻³ = 5 × 10⁻¹⁵ C·m
Torque τ = p × E = pE sinθ; the dipole makes angle with E field; τ = 5 × 10⁻¹⁵ × 1000 × sinθ = 5 × 10⁻¹²  × sinθ

(b)(ii) Initial charges: Q₁ = σ × 4πr₁² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.01)² = 4π × 10⁻⁶ C; Q₂ = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.03)² = 36π × 10⁻⁶ C; Total Q = 40π × 10⁻⁶ C; After connection, same potential: Q₁'/r₁ = Q₂'/r₂; Q₁'/1 = Q₂'/3; Q₁' + Q₂' = 40π × 10⁻⁶; Q₁' = 10π × 10⁻⁶ C = 10π μC

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Consider an electric dipole of moment p placed in a uniform external field E at angle θ. The torque on the dipole is τ = pE sinθ. The work done in rotating the dipole from angle θ₀ to θ is W = ∫τ dθ. Taking θ₀ = 90° as the reference position (where U = 0), the potential energy is U = −pE cosθ = −p·E. The potential energy is (1) maximum when θ = 180° (dipole antiparallel to field): U = +pE, and (2) minimum when θ = 0° (dipole parallel to field): U = −pE.

Part (a)(ii): The dipole consists of −1 pC at (0,0) and +1 pC at (3 mm, 4 mm). The dipole length = √(3² + 4²) = 5 mm = 5 × 10⁻³ m. Dipole moment p = q × d = 1 × 10⁻¹² × 5 × 10⁻³ = 5 × 10⁻¹⁵ C·m. The dipole vector points from −q to +q, i.e., in the direction of (3î + 4ĵ)/5. The torque τ = p × E. Since E = 1000î and p = 5 × 10⁻¹⁵ × (3î + 4ĵ)/5 = 10⁻¹⁵(3î + 4ĵ), τ = 10⁻¹⁵(3î + 4ĵ) × (1000î) = 10⁻¹² × 4(ĵ × î) = −4 × 10⁻¹² k̂ N·m. The magnitude of torque = 4 × 10⁻¹² N·m.

Part (b)(i): The dipole consists of −q at (−a, 0) and +q at (a, 0). The potential at point P(x, 0) where x >> a: V = (1/4πε₀)[q/(x−a) − q/(x+a)] = (q/4πε₀) × [2a/(x²−a²)] ≈ (q/4πε₀) × (2a/x²) = (1/4πε₀) × (p/x²), since p = q × 2a and x >> a means x² − a² ≈ x².

Part (b)(ii): Initial charges: Q₁ = σ × 4πr₁² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.01)² = 4π × 10⁻⁶ C = 4π μC. Q₂ = σ × 4πr₂² = 10⁻² × 4π × (0.03)² = 36π × 10⁻⁶ C = 36π μC. Total charge Q = 40π μC. After connecting by a wire, both spheres reach the same potential: Q₁'/r₁ = Q₂'/r₂, so Q₁'/1 = Q₂'/3, giving Q₂' = 3Q₁'. Also Q₁' + Q₂' = 40π μC → 4Q₁' = 40π μC → Q₁' = 10π μC ≈ 31.4 μC.

(ख) (i) किसी ट्रांसफॉर्मर का नामांकित आरेख खींचकर उसके कार्यकारी सिद्धांत का वर्णन कीजिए। किसी वास्तविक ट्रांसफॉर्मर में होने वाले ऊर्जा ह्रास के किन्हीं तीन कारणों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
(ii) कोई ट्रांसफॉर्मर निम्न वोल्टता को उच्च वोल्टता में परिवर्तित करता है। क्या यह ऊर्जा संरक्षण के सिद्धांत का उल्लंघन करता है? व्याख्या कीजिए।
(iii) किसी ट्रांसफॉर्मर की प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक कुंडलियों में फेरों की संख्या क्रमशः 200 और 3000 है। प्राथमिक कुंडली को दी गई निवेश वोल्टता 90 V है। परिकलित कीजिए: (1) द्वितीयक कुंडली के सिरों पर निर्गत वोल्टता, (2) यदि द्वितीयक कुंडली में धारा 2·0 A है, तो प्राथमिक कुंडली में धारा।
questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series to an ac source v = vm sin ωt. Derive an expression for the impedance of the circuit.
(ii) When does an inductor act as a conductor in a circuit? Give reason for it.
(iii) An electric lamp is designed to operate at 110 V dc and 11 A current. If the lamp is operated on 220 V, 50 Hz ac source with a coil in series, then find the inductance of the coil.
OR
(b) (i) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer and describe its working principle. Explain any three causes for energy losses in a real transformer.
(ii) A step-up transformer converts a low voltage into high voltage. Does it violate the principle of conservation of energy? Explain.
(iii) A step-up transformer has 200 and 3000 turns in its primary and secondary coils respectively. The input voltage given to the primary coil is 90 V. Calculate: (1) The output voltage across the secondary coil, (2) The current in the primary coil if the current in the secondary coil is 2·0 A.

key_points: (a)(i) Impedance Z = √(R² + (1/ωC)²) = √(R² + Xc²)
(a)(ii) Inductor acts as conductor at very high frequency (ω → ∞, X_L = ωL → ∞ is wrong; at dc/very low frequency X_L = ωL → 0, so it acts as a pure conductor)

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): In an RC series circuit connected to v = vm sin ωt, the current leads the voltage across the capacitor. Let current i = im sin(ωt + φ). The voltage across R is v_R = iR (in phase with i), and across capacitor C is v_C = i/ωC (lagging i by 90°). By phasor addition, the net voltage: vm² = (imR)² + (im/ωC)². Therefore im = vm/√(R² + 1/(ωC)²). The impedance Z = vm/im = √(R² + Xc²), where Xc = 1/ωC is the capacitive reactance. The phase angle φ = tan⁻¹(Xc/R).

Part (a)(ii): An inductor acts as a conductor (offers negligible resistance) when the frequency of the ac source is very low or when direct current (dc) flows through it. The inductive reactance X_L = ωL = 2πfL. For dc, f = 0, so X_L = 0, and the inductor behaves like a pure conductor offering only its small ohmic resistance.

Part (a)(iii): Lamp resistance R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω. Operating current must remain 11 A on 220 V ac. Impedance required Z = V_rms/I = 220/11 = 20 Ω. Inductive reactance X_L = √(Z² − R²) = √(400 − 100) = √300 = 10√3 Ω. Inductance L = X_L/ω = 10√3/(2π × 50) = √3/(10π) H ≈ 0.055 H.

Part (b)(i): A step-up transformer has N_s > N_p. The working principle is based on mutual electromagnetic induction. When an ac voltage V_p is applied to the primary coil, it produces a changing magnetic flux in the soft iron core. This changing flux links with the secondary coil and induces an emf V_s = (N_s/N_p) × V_p in it. Three causes of energy losses in a real transformer are: (1) Copper losses (I²R heating in coil wires), (2) Iron/core losses — eddy current losses in the iron core (minimised by lamination), and (3) Hysteresis losses due to repeated magnetisation and demagnetisation of the core.

Part (b)(ii): A step-up transformer does NOT violate the principle of conservation of energy. Although voltage is increased, the current in the secondary decreases proportionally so that the product V × I (power) remains the same (for an ideal transformer). The transformer merely transfers energy from the primary to the secondary circuit; it does not create energy. The power output can never exceed the power input.

Part (b)(iii): (1) V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p → V_s = (3000/200) × 90 = 15 × 90 = 1350 V. (2) For an ideal transformer, V_p I_p = V_s I_s → I_p = (V_s/V_p) × I_s = 15 × 2.0 = 30 A.
